## Introduction

We need to look at recreational data for at least two reasons in the Indicators Project. 

First, we want to groundtruth and possible update recreational catches in the MAB Rpath model for simulation analyses. (MRIP effort and landings have also been rescaled since the model was finalized in 2023.)

Second, to the extent we can include recreational fishery information in the risk policy indicator analysis, the POT would like us to do so.

Here I am downloading existing MRIP data with posting dates 31 August 2026 and evaluating the catches and corresponding uncertainty estimates for MAFMC managed species at the coastwide, Mid-Atlantic, and state (or finer scale) level.


## Methods

Data were downloaded from this website: https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/st1/recreational/MRIP_Survey_Data/CSV/ and each zipped file was saved to a folder in the [indicators-project-data repository](https://github.com/MAFMC/indicators-project-data). MRIP data is all public, I'm storing it here so we know exactly what version of source data we are working with. 

I am referring to the [MRIP handbook](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/s3/2025-03/MRIP-Data-User-Handbook_March_2025_update.pdf.pdf) and the [MRIP Readme](https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/st1/recreational/MRIP_Survey_Data/MRIP-Read-Me.pdf) for usage instructions.

I don't feel confident using these estimates as the columns aren't fully labeled and there are duplicates.

There are template programs here https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/recreational-fishing-data/recreational-fishing-data-downloads#template-programs And several in R here
https://media.fisheries.noaa.gov/2020-04/mrip_catch_estimation_program_template_in_r.zip for catch and here https://media.fisheries.noaa.gov/2020-04/mrip_direct_angler_trip_estimation_template_program_in_r.zip for effort and here
https://media.fisheries.noaa.gov/2022-03/mrip-length-frequencies-template-program-in-r.zip for length frequencies which I hope not to need

There is an R function supplied to do custom estimates from these files (I think) but it is missing a dependency. It may be in the R survey package https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survey/survey.pdf 

We need to separate landings and discards for the recreational fleet for the MAB Rpath model. We need these in weight. 

In a new repository called [indicators-project-data](https://github.com/MAFMC/indicators-project-data) I'm building some code to reproduce how this gets from downloaded csv to model input. Datasets are currently in the `data-raw` folder with the majority of downloaded zip files in an ignored local folder called `ignore_zips` for now. Functions, including the one from the MRIP website, are in the `R` folder. 

As a start I will instead download using the query tool that gives a catch series for the included MAFMC managed species, Atlantic mackerel, black sea bass, bluefish, scup, and summer flounder. I'm trying two downloads, one is total harvest in kg for the Mid-Atlantic [geographic area](https://www.fisheries.noaa.gov/recreational-fishing-data/recreational-fishing-data-glossary#geographical-area) (defined as New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, and Virginia), which is A+B1 and the only series available in total weight. These files are named `mrip_SPECIES_catch_series.csv`and are found in the `data-raw/MRIP` folder of the repository.

The second query gets at the discards as well (released alive, B1) but is available only in numbers of fish. These files are named `mrip_SPECIES_catch_series_N.csv`and are also found in the `data-raw/MRIP` folder of the repository.  For the MAB Rpath model we would require an average weight to use discards in weight in the model, and also a discard mortality rate. Maybe more effort than is needed just for these simulations? But there are a lot of rec releases to consider.... an approximation may be ok.

There is now a function `read_mrip_csv` to read in the catch_series csvs downloaded from the MRIP website that preserves the query options as metadata. It should work on both of these file types.

I've also worked with the provided mrip catch esitmation program template in R, called `MRIP.catch` along with the original data downloaded from https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/st1/recreational/MRIP_Survey_Data/CSV/ to get catch estimates. 

Also there are other downloads, apparently with wave level catch estimates. Here. https://apps-st.fisheries.noaa.gov/st1/recreational/MRIP_Estimate_Data/CSV/Wave%20Level%20Estimate%20Downloads/

These look more similar to what is in the original MAB Rpath repo in formatting so perhaps I can reconstruct the full dataset from these.

We'll compare results across these datasets to see if we get the same answers.

## Test with bluefish

This is a half-baked package with functions and some data, still in development. `IndicatorsProjectData`

The function `IndicatorsProjectData::read_mrip_csv` reads in the bluefish catch series file downloaded directly from the MRIP website. 

```{r}
bluerec <- IndicatorsProjectData::read_mrip_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/mrip_BLUEFISH_catch_series.csv")
```

The metadata from the query is available from `bluerec$params`:

```{r}
bluerec$params
```

We can use the MRIP supplied code to estimate bluefish rec catch for the Mid-Atlantic states using the function `IndicatorsProjectData::MRIP.catch` modified to explicitly call the functions in the R [`survey`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/survey/survey.pdf) package. I've unzipped the files ps_2023_csv.zip, ps_2024_csv.zip, and ps_2025_csv.zip, and renamed their folders to work with the code. The required folder name is `intYYYY` where YYYY is the year. So the folders are called `int2023`, `int2024`, and `int2025`, and are local on my computer at the moment in an ignored folder. 

Then I rearranged the rest of the downloaded files into folders for the `MRIP.catc`h function using code because they were grouped into 10 year blocks in the zip files. See the function `annualfolders` in `indicators-project-data/R`. 

The `MRIP.catch` function is not robust to missing waves, it breaks on 1981, this can be corrected. Trying from 1982-2025.

It is also inadvisable to try it for all the years at once because it is reading them all into a huge dataframe and taking forever. If this finishes (it didnt!) I will save it and if not maybe 5 year blocks are better for this function. This is only one species and I will want to do many.

Lets see if the bluefish totals match for 2023-2025. Note that this calculation sums across all harvest weight values estimated for bluefish by `MRIP.catch`.

They do so try for the whole time series. Eureka.

```{r}
testall <- readRDS(here::here("docs/bluefishrec_testall.rds"))

webquerybluerec <- bluerec$data |>
  dplyr::select(Year, `Harvest (A+B1) Total Weight (kg)`) |>
  dplyr::mutate(Year = as.character(Year))

catchcaldbluerec <- testall |> dplyr::group_by(year) |> 
  dplyr::summarise(harvwtkg = sum(weight)) |> 
  dplyr::select(Year = year, MRIP.catch.weight = harvwtkg) #|>
  #dplyr::mutate(Year = as.numeric(Year))

compblue <- dplyr::left_join(webquerybluerec, catchcaldbluerec)

flextable::flextable(compblue)

```

This suggests I can reproduce the full Mid-Atlantic recreational dataset from the source csvs for the MAB Rpath

What about summing the wave specific catch estimate files? If this gives the same answer it may be easier than doing the calculations.

There are some complications with the wave specific catch estimates. The sums are off by a few kg in either direction for bluefish in the spot checks below. This is not a big deal for the MAB Rpath model because single digit kg differences will not even show up once converted to weight per area, but it would be nicer if results were identical.

```{r}

test <- readr::read_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/ignore_zips/mrip_catch_bywave_2025.csv")

test20 <- readr::read_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/ignore_zips/mrip_catch_bywave_2020.csv")

test1981 <- readr::read_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/ignore_zips/mrip_catch_bywave_1981_1989_csv/mrip_catch_bywave_1981.csv")

test1985 <- readr::read_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/ignore_zips/mrip_catch_bywave_1981_1989_csv/mrip_catch_bywave_1985.csv")

test1989 <- readr::read_csv("/Users/sarahgaichas/Documents/Work/MAFMCindicators/Code/indicators-project-data/data-raw/MRIP/ignore_zips/mrip_catch_bywave_1981_1989_csv/mrip_catch_bywave_1989.csv")

testcatchbywave <- dplyr::bind_rows(test, test20, test1981, test1985, test1989) |>
  dplyr::filter(COMMON == "BLUEFISH",
                ST %in% c(10, 24, 34, 36, 51)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(YEAR) |>
  dplyr::summarise(harvwtkg = sum(WGT_AB1)) |>
  dplyr::select(Year = YEAR, MRIP_bywave = harvwtkg)|>
  dplyr::mutate(Year = as.character(Year))
  

compblue2 <- dplyr::left_join(compblue, testcatchbywave)

flextable::flextable(compblue2)


```
